lecture_summary: The lecture develops nonuniform circular motion by separating radial and tangential acceleration, combining them to determine total acceleration and net-force direction, applying radial/tangential Newton’s-law equations to a ball on a string, and treating the ball as a projectile with tangential initial velocity after the string is cut.

videos.title: Non-Uniform Circular Motion Problems, Centripetal Acceleration & Tangential Acceleration, Physics
videos.reason: Best overall match for distinguishing radial, tangential, and net acceleration and connecting them to changes in velocity direction and speed.

videos.title: Uniform Circular Motion - Calculate Tension Force In a Horizontal & Vertical Circle
videos.reason: Provides the closest force-based string examples, using free-body reasoning and radial Newton’s-law equations with tension and gravity.

videos.title: How To Solve Projectile Motion Problems In Physics
videos.reason: Covers resolving an angled initial velocity and using vertical kinematics to find maximum height—the strategy needed immediately after the string is cut.

coverage_gaps: No playlist video strongly matches the complete arbitrary-angle ball-on-string example: resolving gravity into radial and tangential components, using tension to determine radial acceleration and speed, and then carrying that tangential release speed into a symbolic projectile-height calculation. The selected videos cover these stages separately.
